**A good starting pick is the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh).** The cited estimate says it can run a 100 W ceramic heat emitter on a thermostat for about a day; a low-wattage heat mat should last longer. The listed price is $899, and the page advertises a discount through its [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). ([runtime and product details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

Before buying, check your heater’s wattage and the station’s continuous AC output, and test the setup with your thermostat. Runtime depends on how often the heater switches on, and actual runtime can be lower than a simple capacity estimate. Insulating the enclosure helps conserve heat; Petco also recommends insulation and emergency heat measures during outages. ([Petco’s outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
